notes.title: Game State - Summer 2025
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/78cef1524321ac950aa2760f0bc465c21d97fc18.png"][/img][/p][p]Hello everyone! Thank you for following the development of Dreadshot. I'm a bit late with this post, nevertheless, summer is over, which means it's time to sum it up and lay out plans for the autumn season![/p][h1]What's New?[/h1][p]As usual, let's discuss what tasks were completed during the summer season and which ones remain:[/p][list][*][p] Music System [/p][/*][*][p] [strike]Full implementation of the railgun AK-72[/strike] [/p][/*][*][p] [strike]Full implementation of the new revolver[/strike] [/p][/*][*][p] Full implementation of WMPv2 [/p][/*][*][p] [strike]Full implementation of WM_BOmB[/strike] [/p][/*][*][p] Redesign/Rework of the shotgun, BBHML, and katana for the new animation system[/p][/*][/list][p]3 out of 6 items completed! [/p][h3]Visual Changes[/h3][p]Besides that, I did some work on the game's visuals![/p][p]Namely, I changed the look of the dashes. Here's how it looked before:[/p][previewyoutube="Lu5GEdsPJmo;full"][/previewyoutube][p]And here's how it looks now:[/p][previewyoutube="dQ3w9ktSvGU;full"][/previewyoutube][p]I also updated the robot death effects. Here's how it looked before:[/p][previewyoutube="_VA6Xw3swOA;full"][/previewyoutube][p]And here's how it looks now:[/p][previewyoutube="A2MPmkD6cGo;full"][/previewyoutube][p]There are also some other visual changes, like effects from bullets hitting surfaces, which you can see in the video above.[/p][h2]WMBOmB - A New Enemy Fully in the Game![/h2][p]But all that is just visuals, not that interesting, right? Then let's move on to something hotter... Like WMBOmB.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/c4e7d6e82f3aa8487b212a35cb044ff4d7815e29.gif"][/img][/p][p]I wrote about it in the previous report. There I described its general functionality and what you would be able to do with it. Now, I've added all of it into the game.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="rpGis97nmtw;full"][/previewyoutube][p]WMBOmB is an enemy that will constantly chase the player, and when it gets close, it will jump towards them and explode, dealing significant damage. It's fast and small, making it hard to hit. However, it only takes one hit to make it explode.
Also, if the player is agile enough - they can catch the moment when WMBOmB jumps towards them and kick it in mid-air (if the kick is equipped). Then WMBOmB will fly towards the point where the crosshair is aimed and explode upon impact with a surface.[/p][h2]Revolver Rework[/h2][p]But you know, the explosions from WMBOmB weren't enough for me, so a full revolver rework was implemented: from the model and animations to the mechanics. If before the revolver was quite dull: on RMB (alternate fire) it just quickly fired the entire round with a small spread, which was quite useless and boring, now on RMB (alternate fire) it tosses a pack of dynamite in the direction of the character's movement vector. And the dynamite has huge potential for mechanics. For example, if you shoot it with the revolver - it will break into several smaller dynamite charges that cover a fairly wide area and can help against a crowd of enemies. And if you shoot the dynamite with the BBHML - a more powerful, red explosion will occur, dealing more damage and having a larger area of effect than the regular dynamite explosion, so it can be useful against bosses with a lot of HP. By the way, a regular explosion will occur if you just throw the dynamite and leave it alone. It will explode a couple of seconds after contacting a surface. Well, you can also kick the dynamite like WMBOmB, and it will behave the same way: fly towards the crosshair and explode on contact with a surface. Overall, the revolver turned out to be extremely interesting and functional, however, it still needs attention. At the very least, I need to figure out a system for reloading the dynamite. For now, I'm leaning towards the dynamite being usable once every 5 seconds, and it will passively recharge, but I might change that.[/p][previewyoutube="gE_Q1cIePi0;full"][/previewyoutube][h2]AK-72 is Now in the Game![/h2][p]I didn't limit myself to just the revolver when updating the arsenal. So, I finally fully implemented the AK-72 assault rifle, which I also talked about in the last seasonal report. The only thing is, I changed the mechanic: hitting enemies charges the cores for the railgun. There are 3 cores total, and the more cores charged - the more powerful the railgun shot will be, both in damage and explosion radius. Yes, all railgun shots create an explosion, the size of which depends on the charge level of the core. The system is quite smart because if you have, say, 2.5 cores charged, only 2 cores will be spent, and 0.5 will be saved, so you'll only need to charge another half to fire the railgun. By the way, the AK-72 is currently the only weapon that has spread. I didn't add spread to other weapons to make the game less dependent on RNG, and also because the weapons up to this point were only semi-automatic. If the AK-72 had no spread - it would be a dumb laser gun that would be too easy to shoot. So, there is spread, but it's not constant. It gradually expands depending on how long the weapon has been firing non-stop. And if you stop firing even for half a second - the spread will gradually return to its original state, and you can continue accurate fire. For exactly the same reason, because it's an automatic rifle - I added a slight distortion to the firing sound when the magazine is low on ammo. This is done so the player can determine the remaining ammo by sound without looking at the interface. I liked this feature so much that I also added it to pistols that fire fast enough, making it sometimes hard to keep track of the ammo count. I think the AK-72, thanks to its railgun, has very good potential for interaction with other weapons, for example with BBHML rockets and the revolver's dynamite. Besides that, there might be potential for movement, as explosions created by the player don't damage them, and you could use the railgun explosion to gain speed.[/p][previewyoutube="Q46R23zxntw;full"][/previewyoutube][h2]Game Optimization[/h2][p]For the most part, that's all the new stuff that was added, but there's one more thing... Game optimization. I started noticing that the average FPS in the game began to drop, and stutters became more frequent, which are quite annoying. I already have some assumptions about why this is happening and a rough idea of how to fix it, even though it will take quite a lot of time. I won't go into technical details here, I'll just say that game optimization is an extremely important task, and I will try to make it as good as possible within my capabilities.[/p][h2]Game Funding[/h2][p]There's also another piece of good news: the project has received quite stable funding! It's all thanks to my media profiles on social networks; I got advertisers there, and the revenue from them provides me with the necessary minimum to fund my game. This means I can now devote all my free time to working on the game and its content, which is very encouraging.[/p][h2]What's Next?[/h2][p]The plans for the autumn season are Napoleonic (ambitious). We need to consider that I only have 2 out of 3 months free, as I have university exams in November, which will take a significant amount of energy and time. So, during September and October, I need to try to complete as many of the following tasks as possible:[/p][list][*][p][b]Music System[/b] [/p][/*][*][p][b]Full implementation of WMPv2[/b] [/p][/*][*][p][b]Redesign/Rework of the shotgun, BBHML, and katana for the new animation system[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Enemy spawn/respawn system, spawners[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Reduce the number of dependencies between objects in the game for the sake of optimization[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Add more weapons[/p][/*][*][p]Add more enemies besides WMPv2[/p][/*][*][p][b]Start designing levels for the story campaign[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Main character model (for promo + cutscenes)[/p][/*][*][p]Fully write the game's story[/p][/*][*][p]Weapon and skills merchant model[/p][/*][*][p]Create a skill upgrade system[/p][/*][*][p]Rework the shop from a terminal to a weapon merchant's stall[/p][/*][*][p]Hub location that will be between levels[/p][/*][*][p]Cutscene system[/p][/*][*][p]Dialogue and subtitle system[/p][/*][/list][p]Obviously, I won't do all of this in 2 months; these are plans for the next 2-3 seasons. However, these are the plans that need to be accomplished to bring the game to the early access stage and start sales of that early access. The highlighted items are the priority items; after their implementation, it will be possible, in principle, to start open free playtests of the game on Steam. That's why I will start with the highlighted items and then move on to the others.[/p][h3]Wishlists[/h3][p]By tradition, wishlists! And they are as follows: the game is on the wishlist of 6,610 (-34) people! I didn't do any wishlist marketing this season, so a small decline happened, but it's not critical.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you for continuing to follow the project's development and for reading this article! See you at the beginning of winter![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/06635c9651cb2dde72edf86d8d70d356be7336a9.jpg"][/img][/p][p][url="https://skfb.ly/oFUX6"]Coctail model used for render[/url][/p]

notes.title: Game State - Spring 2025
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/6f61b4412bbb1866f29c066fa2675847e97cf6dd.png[/img]
Hello to everyone who follows Dreadshot! Summer is just around the corner, which means it's time to sum up the results of spring, or more precisely, what happened with the game during the spring period. A lot has happened, but let's take it one step at a time.

As usual, let's discuss which of the previously set goals were achieved this season:
[list]
[*][strike]At least 1 mid-range weapon[/strike]
[*]Add all missing objects to the map editor
[*]Music system
[*][strike]1-2 more enemy NPCs, in addition to WMPv1[/strike]
[/list]
I crossed out two of the four goals. But the catch is that they are not fully implemented, they are currently only at the concept stage. I crossed them out because coming up with a complete concept is the most difficult part of adding new content, at least for me personally.
In addition to the tasks that were set, other work was also done in the game (and outside of it):
[list]
[*] Kill reload system
[*] WMPv1 AI optimization
[*] Dynamic camera when moving sideways
[*] Updated Steam page
[*] Many different sounds have been changed and added
[*] Added the ability to blow up an enemy's flying projectile with a revolver shot
[*] Updated UE version from 5.4.4 to 5.5.4
[*] Added speed rings
[*] Created models for new enemies: WMPv2 and WMBOmB (working title)
[*] Completely remade the revolver and pistol
[*] Reworked the animation system for weapons
[*] Created a concept for a new mid-range weapon: Rail AK-72 (working title)
[*] In early/mid-spring, active work was underway on TikTok to promote the game
[/list]

Yes, a lot of third-party work was done. Let me tell you about the most interesting points from the list above.
[h2]
Kill reload system[/h2]
The reload system is designed to solve two problems: reloading itself (namely its long animations) and the use of only one weapon. The system works in such a way that if you don't have a full magazine in your weapon, and you switch to another weapon, then kill an enemy with it, the ammunition is automatically restored on all weapons. Thus, if you constantly change weapons and kill enemies with different weapons, reloading will not be a problem for you, and you will be able to increase your effectiveness in combat.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/af9de9839aa8024c0fb3c98ed1e2d2b62d5bca53.gif[/img]

[h2]Dynamic camera when moving sideways[/h2]
I won't hide it: this improvement was blatantly taken from Ultrakill. But it fits so well with the dynamics of the gameplay that I really wanted to include it. Of course, you can disable it (or enhance it) if you don't like the standard sway.

Standard sway:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/5a01bc1e204c524bf8aabb35ba8fdd751174231e.gif[/img]

Without sway:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/a0b5360bbd1a973c60de0d70dc6cc460da955e87.gif[/img]

х2 sway:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/035633f32c380b95142142c5fe48a0313ed5bd69.gif[/img]

[h2]Acceleration rings added[/h2]
Acceleration rings are another element of the environment that can be used to move around the map efficiently. The ring always gives momentum in the direction of the player's gaze. It doesn't matter where the player was moving before flying through the ring — they will always receive momentum in the direction of their gaze, whether it's down or up. Due to the fact that these rings knock down aim on targets, they are unlikely to be used often in combat arenas, but will rather be used in parkour segments between arenas.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/27b09c0f2fa93ee777daa0bfd8acf03e4549a557.gif[/img]

[h2]Models created for new enemies: WMPv2 and WMBOmB[/h2]
[h3]WMPv2[/h3]
WMPv2 is a logical continuation of WMPv1. It is a very similar model with almost identical behavior. The only difference is the firing rate. While WMPv1 fires a single-shot blaster that needs to be reloaded for 5 seconds after each shot, WMPv2 fires an automatic blaster and fires a burst of bullets for several seconds before reloading. It has not been implemented in the game yet, only the model exists, but in essence, adding it will not be difficult, since its AI is very similar to WMPv1.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/b377df89ab2cb9b1ccd43fe9cfd1d88fd3b464ea.jpg[/img]

[h3]WM_BOmB[/h3]
WM_BOmB is an amusing case, by the way. During one of my sick days, while running a high fever, I had a dream about this head on legs with dynamite in its teeth, and I realized that it would actually make an excellent enemy. It will encourage the player to move around more and stand still less, because if the player stays in one place, WM_BOmB will run up and explode.
WM_BOmB will also have various other uses. For example, it can be kicked with your foot, and it will fly in the direction of the camera's gaze and explode at the point where it stops (whether it's an enemy or a wall). Or you can just shoot it, and it will explode immediately with one shot.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/c8082a0d3f3593141448ec7863e7178ac10be187.jpg[/img]

[h2]Completely remade revolver and pistol[/h2]
[h3]Pistol.[/h3]
Yes, two weapons have been completely remade. Let's start with the pistol.
The pistol used to be a very ordinary gun with no special features. It wasn't bad, but it was too boring, and most players would probably replace the pistol with any other weapon. But now it's not just one pistol, but two.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/fcec8c0200c99dbb0cd488052fbb582d2ccbb4bb.png[/img]
The point is that one pistol can automatically target a pre-selected enemy. The player, after targeting the enemy, can press the right mouse button, and the left pistol's crosshair will automatically target the selected enemy, and each shot will deal damage to that enemy, regardless of the player's crosshair. This way, the player can either increase the speed of killing one enemy by reducing the number of potential misses, or shoot at two enemies at once.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/8b15860df96c6d78b751b05b80f23823a35038f3.gif[/img]
[h3]Revolver.[/h3]
The revolver is not yet ready for the game, but some of the mechanics for it have already been created. The point is that previously, the revolver simply fired its entire magazine in a row as an alternative shot. I decided that this was rather boring and not very effective. So I replaced the alternative shot with throwing dynamite. By pressing the right mouse button while using the revolver, the player can throw dynamite. It flies with roughly the same physics as a coin in Ultrakill. The dynamite explodes passively one second after bouncing off the surface. Dynamite will also explode immediately if it is hit by a rocket or an enemy shot, and the explosion will be amplified. Dynamite can also be kicked with your foot, in which case it will fly forward, just like the aforementioned WM_BOmB, and explode immediately upon hitting the surface. In general, dynamite is quite functional, and in the future it will be interesting to combine it with almost any other weapon.
The revolver itself has been redesigned.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/03eefc8abea921d95fbc5401d17498cf03fd1903.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/9e4ffea2d0bb667921dc229843c2814717c02d57.jpg[/img]

[h2]Concept created for a new mid-range weapon: Rail AK-72[/h2]
This assault rifle took too long to create. I understood that everyone loves assault rifles in games: they are versatile and practical. But I needed to make an assault rifle that wouldn't overshadow all other weapons, but would harmonize with the entire arsenal. I'm not sure if I succeeded, but I tried my best, and I will change it in the future if necessary.
In short, I find the mechanics of the machine gun quite interesting. The idea is that when you fire the machine gun, you fill your enemies with potential energy. The more energy they have, the more damage they will take from an alternate shot. An alternate shot is a shot from the rail that consumes half of the machine gun's energy, but deals more damage the more potential charge there is on the enemy.
The two barrels at the bottom are the main barrels, from which the main barrel will fire. They will fire alternately. The design is engineered with “anti-recoil” in mind, so the barrels will slide nicely into the machine gun when firing. By the way, I don't care at all that this will have no effect in real life; I do everything with an emphasis on style, not realism.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/dd11b20f103f4c6dd470fb93d345b1df0fb095e1.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/05d9d97beac1745cc287f1455cebb59e394d7dca.jpg[/img]

[h2]What's next?[/h2]
Next up is the summer period. During the summer, we need to work even harder and focus on polishing what we've added so far, as well as finishing up any unfinished aspects. So, the tasks are:
[list]
[*] Music system
[*] Full implementation of the rail AK-72
[*] Full implementation of the new revolver
[*] Full implementation of WMPv2
[*] Full implementation of WM_BOmB
[*] Redesign/rework of the shotgun, BBHML, and katana for the new animation system
[/list]

The goals are quite modest and, in my opinion, more than achievable. I need to focus on them and strive to create all the conditions necessary to start designing gameplay levels and, along with them, publish an open gameplay test of the game for everyone interested in order to gather more feedback. And so you don't miss it, add the game to your wish list!

Speaking of wish lists... The game is on the wish list of 6,644 people (+1,190).

Thank you all for reading, see you at the end of summer!

notes.title: Game State - Winter 2025
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/2544a01396c93fbc14e86859aedc561ff9b48635.png[/img]
Hello everyone! Winter is ending, and with it we need to summarize the results of this period. To tell you the truth, I'm surprised how fast the time flew by, because I wrote the fall "Game State" as if it was yesterday. But that's not the point

Let's talk about what goals were accomplished this season:
[list]
[*][strike]At least 1 melee weapon[/strike]
[*]At least 1 mid-range weapon
[*][strike]Tidying up the sandbox test location[/strike].
[*]Adding all missing objects to the map editor
[*]Music system
[*]1-2 more enemy NPCs besides WMPv1
[/list].

Only 2 goals out of 6 completed. Not enough? I guess. But the work that wasn't listed in the objectives was done. For example:
[list]
[*] Added some decorative functional objects (interactive buttons, sources of settling, text banners).
[*] Added water and the ability to swim in it (still in test mode)
[*] Significantly revised mechanics of dash and grapple-hook: they are now more predictable and convenient in real gameplay, and they can no longer be abused to gain impossible speeds.
[*] The game HUD has been completely changed and a bunch of nice animations have been added to it.
[*] There were a lot of improvements and bugfixes that make the game more pleasant.
[/list]

But the coolest thing is of course the new melee weapons. Namely, fists. Yes, it may not sound very cool when there is already a katana as a melee weapon, but fists have their own chips.
For example, fists are capable of hitting combos with quick punches on the LMB, and making a finishing blow on pressing the RMB, which does more damage the more punches you hit with quick punches. It also throws the enemy into the air, using the same system: more hits - stronger throws. The most interesting thing is that if a player jumps up right before the finishing hit, they will fly up with the enemy when making the finishing hit, and will be able to perform a chain of combos in the air until the unfortunate enemy dies.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/46c7ba9a8f656c81063a376aaecf1633c6770bc8.png[/img]
Also, a feature of all weapons in the melee class is the ability to use them quickly. So, with a katana, you can strike quickly without switching weapons. At the same time, if the strike hits at the moment a projectile hits you - the projectile will be reflected. Yes, yes, it will be[i] parried[/i]. Fists, on the other hand, have a different quick strike. It is done not with the fists, but with the foot, and it has a lot of uses.
The leg is capable of throwing back enemies, and if the player was in the air at the moment of the hit, they will be thrown back, no matter whether the player hit the enemy or some surface. In fact, you can push off of anything with your foot, thus easily gaining height.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/e9e6ad904a0e32aa60e4e669e3f3a9ecfbb5c125.png[/img]
Overall: the fists turned out interesting, but more work needs to be done on them, gather feedback, and make the adjustments this weapon needs.

Speaking of work: I quit my job! This means that in the near future (2-3 months) I will be able to fully devote myself to game development and content creation, which is a great thing.

What else I'm excited about in this update is the new Sandbox mode location. When I made it, I had two goals: functionality and beauty. I achieved beauty with nice lighting and effects on the location, but functionality is possible thanks to modularity. Basically, the location is a cylinder, inside of which you can make different passages, and in each passage you can make a separate room. Thanks to this, you can make a lot of different rooms, where the most different mechanics of the game will be tested.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/4ac184e00ebc5ae7dec709e63d6b52119099b816.jpg[/img]

That's it for now. As I said in the last report - we are working on letting players try out the free one-week test, collect as much feedback as possible, and work from there. As usual, I won't promise when that will be. I'd like it as soon as possible, of course, but I can't promise that at the moment.

Conclusions:
[olist].
[*] Added a lot of things that weren't mentioned in the predetermined goals
[*] Completed 2 out of 6 goals
[*] Remaining goals should be tried to close during the spring, as there is free time.
[*] The best changes of the season are the fists and the new sandbox location.
[*] The game is on the vishlist of 5,454 people (-20).
[/olist]

Thank you all so much for your support, testing (who have the INDEV closed version), and donations for the development of the game. Have a great spring holidays, and we'll see you at the end of May!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/6a4f92e917c77148df310024245158f40da3b985.jpg[/img]
[spoiler]The picture above is a pre-render, these animations are not in the game.[/spoiler]

notes.title: Game State - Fall 2024
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/b3b153dcbee50c9788908a5b00863f7d4aa69f16.png[/img]
Hi everyone!!! Here fall has passed, which means it's time to take stock of this season. Despite my rather heavy workload during this period (I had a session in uni, and also went to work for hire) - Dreadshot still transformed quite well in my opinion. But, let's go in order.

Let's remember what the immediate goals were at the time of writing the previous article:
[list]
[*] [strike]Enemy AI[/strike]
[*] [strike]At least 1 heavy class weapon[/strike]
[*] At least 1 melee weapon.
[*] At least 1 medium weapon
[*] Tidying up the sandbox test location.
[*] [strike]Restore the map editor[/strike] and add all missing objects to it.
[*] Music system
[*] 1-2 more enemy NPCs, besides WMPv1
[/list]

As you can understand, 3/8 of the goals are completed, and that's pretty good considering my workload in real life, and the fact that this season has seen a lot of work done to polish the already existing mechanics and systems in the game. This included fixing about 30-50 bugs, both critical and not-so-critical. Minimal changes were also made to the interface design.

The hardest part was developing the AI for WMPv1, as I hadn't done anything like that before. Eventually an AI came out that can shoot, hide, come out of cover, shoot from around a corner, search for the player, and return to the starting position. It's still not perfect, there's a huge amount of room for polishing, but for the first time, until there aren't even normal levels - it's quite a workable option.

The most interesting thing to add was probably the first heavy class weapon, the BBHML.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/9e7b159d71643f850ce9941f54de751fe3215896.jpg[/img]
The BBHML is a four-shot rocket launcher with homing missiles. The missiles always fly to the point the player is looking at. The missiles can also be detonated in advance, before colliding with the target. Thanks to this, the missiles can be detonated immediately after being fired, thus giving themselves acceleration in the air without any auxiliary surfaces.
In general, the rocket launcher is fun and interesting to play, it has a huge potential for both attack and muvement.

For the winter, the plans remain the same as in the list above. Work is underway to release the game in a week-long open test on Steam, and if we continue at this pace, it could very well be by the end of winter or sometime in the spring. I can't promise anything, this is just speculation. I want to give people a taste of the project as much as possible in this situation, and that takes a lot of time and preparation, because after all, I make practically nothing from its development, and I'm quite severely limited in time. 

[h1]Conclusions[/h1]
[olist]
[*] In the fall season a lot of bugs and errors were fixed, and new content was added in the form of AI for WMPv1 and BBHML rocket launcher.
[*] The winter season will continue with the fulfillment of the previous tasks.
[*] The game is on the vishlist of 5,474 (-72) people.
[/olist]

Thank you all so much for your support of development, for your attention, it's definitely important for morale! See you in February <3
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/ab0eea53eb558caee2fe554ce0c2c8145d56fcbc.png[/img]

notes.title: Game State - Summer 2024
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44925915/22f77107ff1cd2a8e01e79899d5da39e3a884d15.png[/img]
[h1]Hello everyone![/h1] In order to have a closer contact with the audience - it was decided to give news about the game's development and content right here in the Steam community, so that you won't miss anything. Today, as the first post of this kind, I will tell you what is in the game at the moment, what content has been added and/or changed over the summer period, as well as share the nearest plans for the next season.
Also, I think it's a good idea to share the exact number of whishlists for the game in each such post. At the moment, the game is on the wishlist of [b]5546[/b] people!

[h1]What content is currently available in the closed version of the game?[/h1]
[list]
[*] Main Menu
[*] Game Settings
[*] Sandbox level for testing all mechanics.
[*] 1 melee weapon (katana)
[*] 2 light class weapons (pistol and revolver)
[*] 1 medium weapon (shotgun)
[*] 1 almost functional enemy NPC (in development)
[*] Speedrun mode
[*] Map Editor (temporarily disabled at the moment)
[*] Test dummies
[*] Targets for shooting practice
[*] More than a dozen interactive objects (exploding barrels, breaking glass, moving platforms, jump panels, interactive doors, equipment store, and so on)
[/list]

[h1]Predictions for the fall season[/h1]
[h1]Lower productivity in the fall[/h1]
The fall is expected to be less productive. Development has been done for the last year with an extremely small budget (about $100/month on average). I made a very large bet on this project, and have not been officially employed for a year now. During this season, development has progressed quite a bit compared to the same summer in 2023. However, I physically can't continue like this, I need money for my basic human existence, and I'm not even talking about the fact that I also need money to buy hardware and software for game development. That's why I'm moving game development back to a hobby format in the fall, and will be doing it less constantly. I will note that this is exactly a reduction in activity, but not a complete stop. The development will still continue, but it will be less active. And so it will be until I will not have from the game a permanent monthly income of at least 300-400$ per month (which is the average actual salary in my country).
